children: The S&P 500 closed Wednesday at 7,706, just over 1% below its August 13 record peak of 7,799, maintaining solid year-to-date and 12-month gains of 13% and 16%, respectively. This sets up the central tactical question for investors: whether current price action represents a routine consolidation beneath all-time highs or the early stages of a fresh leg higher.

Sustaining further gains hinges on fundamental execution. Upward revisions to 2026 earnings estimates and resilient AI capital expenditure continue to anchor EPS growth, even as most Wall Street year-end targets imply only modest upside from current levels.

Historical seasonality also provides a tailwind. While September has averaged a 0.7% decline over the past 25 years, the market is entering its strongest seasonal quarter, led by November, which has averaged a 2.6% gain with an 83% win rate.

Underpinning market strength, the information technology sector represents nearly one-third of the S&P 500, and it is finding firmer footing as semiconductors attempt to forge a support floor while software displays relative outperformance. However, macro headwinds remain active. The 10-year Treasury yield trades near two-decade highs, crude oil continues to flirt with $100, and hot flash PMI prints present a double-edged sword, fueling corporate earnings while undercutting the 'Fed pause' narrative.

Concurrently, market breadth has narrowed as the cap-weighted benchmark sits within 1% of its record high, the Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF remains 5% off its peak, pacing toward its first six-week losing streak since mid-2022. The technical parameters below map the projected path should the August peak be taken out to the upside.

Looking at the daily chart, the S&P 500 ratio chart against the Nasdaq has lagged since August, mirroring the April-May period and signaling that relative market strength favors growth over value. Broad momentum began with a rare gap up on April 8 rising 2.5% and forcefully reclaiming both the 50-day and 200-day simple moving averages in a single session.

That initial momentum established a bull flag formation beginning at the very round 7,000 level. The 7,500 level was briefly undercut during a late July shakeout, but the index mounted a rapid recovery in early August, carving out a multi-week double-bottom base that established a key breakout trigger at 7,757.

Price action cleared that 7,757 pivot on September 21 with a 1.5% gain, but the breakout stalled immediately. Because high-quality technical resolutions typically demand swift follow-through, Wednesday's completion of a bearish evening star introduces short-term risk. Nevertheless, the pattern maintains an ultimate measured target of 8,050 by early 2027-about 5% upside from Thursday's trading level-provided the index holds above 7,600.
The S&P 500 was trading around 7,665 Thursday.

Turning to the weekly chart, a bearish MACD crossover introduces an important tactical caution signal. Historical precedent underscores this indicator's relevance. The prior two occurrences, across December 2024 and November 2025, signaled multi-week cool-offs that ultimately pulled the index back toward the upward-sloping 50-week simple moving average.

Counterbalancing this momentum divergence, the index deserves credit for defending its weekly bull flag breakout. However, a clustering of recent doji candles highlights underlying indecision and frequently precedes trend shifts. While price action remains the ultimate authority over secondary indicators, a decisive breakdown below 7,500 would open the door to a deeper mean-reversion move toward the 50-week moving average.

As long as structural support holds, the primary path of least resistance remains skewed to the upside. The long-term measured move originating from the weekly bull flag breakout points toward 8,600 by year-end 2027-12% upside potential from current levels-offering an attractive long-term horizon for trend-following strategies.

Doug Busch is the senior technical analyst at Barron's Investor Circle. His technical view is added to stock picks, including those published exclusively for Investor Circle readers. A glossary of technical terms is updated regularly with new entries.
